claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch on the current record because aggregate readiness passed, rollout controls limit blast radius, and the remaining enterprise refund-policy summarization weakness can be handled by disclosing it in launch documentation rather than blocking certification.
decision_criteria: Policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
Aggregate readiness passing and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch readiness, but not waiver of the disclosure requirement.
An approved, specific risk acceptance or completed launch disclosure would materially strengthen support for certification.
evidence_requests: Provide the launch model card or launch packet showing the enterprise refund-policy summarization limitation is explicitly disclosed.
Provide approval or publication evidence that the disclosure will be present at launch.
If relying on risk acceptance instead of disclosure, provide an approved risk-acceptance document that specifically addresses enterprise refund workflow exposure.
specific_concerns: The admissible evidence supports a conditional conclusion only: certification is plausible if the enterprise refund limitation is actually disclosed at launch.
There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure has been completed or approved before launch.
The affected enterprise refund workflow remains exposed in the initial cohort, so rollout controls do not substitute for disclosure under the policy text.
The risk-acceptance draft is unapproved and does not cover the exposed enterprise refund segment, so it cannot cure the disclosure predicate.
unsupported_claims: The recommended action 'certify_model' is not fully supported as an unconditional present-tense action on the current record because required disclosure is only described, not evidenced.
Any implication that rollout controls plus monitoring are enough on their own to justify certification would be unsupported by the policy and evidence.
